data.content:
Mathspace breach hits 1 million students and parents in Australia and NZ.  Attackers used a known Metabase flaw that’s already caught other companies this summer. No passwords taken, but watch for fake “your child’s account” emails.

#cybersecurity #databreach #mathspace #phishing #techreels

Flown to or through Vietnam since 2017? 220 million traveller records, passport numbers, seat numbers and baggage tags included, were sitting online behind a default password. Scanners spotted the server in 2022. It was fixed in June. No logs, so nobody knows who else got in. Would you have tapped that email? 
#cybersecurity #databreach #vietnam #travel #techtok

Someone’s been calling cyber creators LARPers for not being technical enough. I keep cyber simple, so you can guess where I land.

You don’t have to be technical to work in cyber. Over 60% of incidents start with a human, and no product fixes that.

Simple is a choice, and it’s harder than hiding behind jargon.

#cybersecurity #cyberawareness #cyberlarp #contentcreator #keepcybersimple

The software protecting millions of work laptops just became the way in. A researcher has released a working CrowdStrike Falcon exploit that hands attackers full SYSTEM control on fully patched Windows 11. CrowdStrike is investigating. The same person has hit Kaspersky, Avast and Microsoft this year. Should vendors be threatening researchers, or paying them?

#crowdstrike #cybersecurity #windows #techreels #cybernews

A hefty breach at an ID provider. I said on the podcast over a year ago, the day the Online Safety Act came into force that we needed a list of providers and a standard. Nobody ever built the list or the standard. 153 million driving licences later, here we are. Why keep hold of them?

#CyberSecurity #DataBreach #OnlineSafetyAct #DarkWeb #techreels

Dropbox trusted a login system it didn’t control, and 5,000 people paid for it. Got 2FA switched on everywhere that matters? 

#CyberSecurity #DataBreach #Dropbox #lenovo #techreels

MAG said no to the ransom, so the hackers dumped 8.7 million records online instead. Here’s what’s actually in the data, and what to watch out for if you’ve flown through Manchester Airport, Stansted Airport or East Midlands. 

#cybersecurity #databreach #manchesterairport #phishing #stansted

Plex is pushing this update harder than usual, and most people still won’t rush to install it. The last time a Plex update got ignored, it took three years and cost a password manager its entire customer vault. Are you the type to update straight away, or let it sit?

Hashtags: #CyberSecurity #Plex #lastpass #updates #techreels

Windows users are being asked to ignore a message that their AV is turned off. I wonder if they’ll be told when they no longer have to ignore it? #microsoft #windows #antivirus #techreels #cybersecurity

Jersey police say 75% of scam reports in one month were Revolut related. One phone call, one “safe account” request, thousands gone. Has anyone here had one of these calls?

#CyberSecurity #ScamAlert #Revolut #techreels #StaySafeOnline

Anthropic just warned Claude users their sessions were hijacked, not by a Claude flaw, but by malware already on their PC. Credit to them for actually emailing users about it. And fake GTA 6 downloads are one of the biggest sources of that malware right now. Have you checked your active sessions lately?

#CyberSecurity #InfoStealer #techreels #GTA6 #claude

This Claude skill clones a website pixel for pixel in one prompt, and it just made building phishing sites really easy. Is this really the new phishing threat? 
#CyberSecurity #AI #Phishing #Techreels #Claude

Google just paid $10m for 100 million emails and 500 million Teams chats from bankrupt Spirit Airlines. Names get stripped, tone doesn’t. Would your work Slack survive the deidentification test?

#CyberSecurity #DataPrivacy #AI #techreels #GoogleAI

Rockstar’s takedown team can’t keep up. A new leak suggests someone has a playable build of GTA 6, seven days before the official reveal. Do you think this hurts the launch or hypes it?

#GTA6 #RockstarGames #GamingNews #Leak #techreels

Monzo went down today. Most customers didn’t feel it, because there’s a second bank running quietly behind the first one. The 803+ hours of combined outages across nine UK banks is real, verified Treasury Committee data, covering Jan 2023 to Feb 2025, not the current two years. Would you trust your bank more if you knew it had a backup like this?

#CyberSecurity #Monzo #Fintech #aws #Techreels

The UK’s new AI minister lost the one job that actually protects you from it, three weeks after getting promoted. To be clear, Narayan’s track record on this brief was genuinely strong, this isn’t about him. Safeguarding doesn’t sit with a minister now, it sits within a wider department with competing priorities.

Credit to @dr_catherine_knibbs for the reel tag that started this.

What do you think, should safeguarding have its own dedicated minister, or is folding it into a department with competing priorities the right call?

#AI #UKPolitics #OnlineSafety #Safeguarding #Cybersecurity

Apple’s suing OpenAI over stolen secrets, but its own iCloud setup might be the real leak. Ever checked what’s syncing on your work Mac?

#cybersecurity #apple #databreach #openai #techreels

Google built SynthID to prove what’s AI. Then launched a feature that made it pointless, on the one platform people actually trusted. Would you have noticed if it wasn’t pulled?

Blast crater example via @404mediaco

#Google #AI #misinformation #Cybersecurity #techreels

Anthropic pirated millions of ebooks, got sued for it, then found a legal way to do the same thing: buy the book, shred it, keep the text. So why won’t AI recite the exact copyrighted lines it was trained on? Project Panama is its name!

#Anthropic #AI #Copyright #Piracy #techreels

Saw a video calling out ExpressVPN, PIA, CyberGhost, ZenMate, NordVPN and Surfshark as some of the worst VPNs for privacy. So I checked every claim myself. Some of it holds up. Most of it doesn’t. Full breakdown in the video.

#cybersecurity #vpn #privacy #techreels #cyber

TP-Link, the FCC, and a ban that only sort of exists. Worth knowing before your next router purchase.

#CyberSecurity #TPLink #FCC #Techtok #Router

Anthropic just confirmed three of its Claude models broke into real companies during cybersecurity testing, weeks after OpenAI’s own containment breach at Hugging Face. One built and uploaded a malicious Python package that ran on 15 real systems before anyone noticed.

#cybersecurity #ai #claude #openai #techreels

Waze’s terms and conditions change on August 1st. I’ve seen videos calling it shocking. I read the actual document. Here’s what’s really in it, and what should actually worry you about navigation apps.

#Waze #DataPrivacy #techreels #Cybersecurity #GPS

Juice jacking has scared phone users for over a decade. Zero documented real world cases. Here’s what your phone actually protects you from, and the one new twist that means the advice isn’t completely dead yet.

#CyberSecurity #Techreels #JuiceJacking #iphone #android

Hundreds of private Claude chats ended up searchable on Google, legal questions, crypto wallet keys, medical details. Anthropic says they fixed this once already. Breaking down why that fix might not actually be holding, and why it’s happened to three different AI companies now.

#cybersecurity #AI #Claude #DataPrivacy #techreels

75 million Revolut records allegedly for sale. Revolut says there’s no breach. Here’s why these claims are so hard to trust, with a few other examples that never checked out.

#CyberSecurity #Revolut #DataBreach #Fintech #techreels

Got an Android phone and have ads popping up right after you hang up the phone? There’s a reason, and it’s not a glitch. Full breakdown in the video.

#CyberSecurity #android #ScamAlert #techreels #StaySafeOnline

Steam forums are getting hit with fake “fixes” that quietly install cryptominers. If you ran a PowerShell command from a forum reply recently, check for this.

#CyberSecurity #Gaming #Steam #techreels #Malware

Public Wi-Fi paranoia was debunked for good reason, encryption stops people sniffing your traffic. But this ReliaQuest report from 23 July shows a different attack entirely: hijacked hotel and conference Wi-Fi DNS, redirecting travellers to fake Microsoft 365 logins, some bypassing MFA without stealing a single password. Hotels and venues need to take security serious but for normal travellers, the fix is one VPN setting. (VPN companies, my inbox is open.)

#cybersecurity #phishing #vpn #hotelwifi #techreels

A hacker wiped Romania’s entire land registry with one stolen password. Every property record in the country, gone overnight.

But the story I keep thinking about isn’t Romania. It’s what happens if that’s the UK Land Registry. Or HMRC. Or NHS records.

We don’t think about these systems until they disappear. Maybe we should.

#CyberSecurity #CriticalInfrastructure #hacking #Infosec #techreels

Your WhatsApp messages were readable by any website you visited this week. Not because WhatsApp was hacked. Because Adobe added a WhatsApp integration to a browser extension you probably forgot you had installed.

This is HermeticReader, and why everything integrating with everything is a security problem waiting to happen.

#CyberSecurity #WhatsApp #Adobe #BrowserExtensions #techreels

OpenAI’s AI escaped its box, hacked Hugging Face, and triggered a congressional kill switch bill. But the real story is what happened when Hugging Face tried to defend themselves. American AI refused to help. So they called in a Chinese model. And now everyone is being told to keep one on standby.

#openai #ai #cybersecurity #congress #techreels

An AI broke out of its own sandbox last week and hacked into a real company’s systems. Everyone’s calling it a failure. I’m not sure that’s the whole story. #AI #cybersecurity #openai #huggingface #techreels

CVEs are how the security world tracks vulnerabilities. One flaw, one number, one shared language that everything from your antivirus to your patch manager runs on.

Your phone has them. Your router has them. A coffee maker had one.

What CVE actually means, how to read one, and why the system nearly disappeared without most people noticing.

#CyberSecurity #CVE #InfoSec #techtips #techreels

Microsoft are laying things to rest in October. Publisher after 35 years. Office LTSC 2021. Windows Server mainstream support. And an Entra ID retirement that has real teeth if you miss it. Whether you’re someone with a life or buried deep in IT, this one has something for everyone. 

#Microsoft #CyberSecurity #windows #EntraID #techreels

Someone flagged something odd about Lovable this week. So I looked into it.

While the agent is working... it’s sometimes thinking in Chinese.

Not the output. The output is fine. The internal reasoning. Chinese characters.

This is documented behaviour across multiple AI reasoning models. Chinese characters are more token-efficient. Some models just... do it. Because the training points that way.

But the real story is the supply chain underneath. Which model is actually running? Which inference provider? Where do the reasoning traces go?

Most security teams don’t even know their people are using these tools.

#CyberSecurity #AI #VibeCoding #lovable #techreels

432 CVEs in 24 hours from the Linux kernel. The number is big. The crisis isn’t real.

The kernel runs its own CVE authority and publishes everything when a stable release drops. Fix-first model means patches ship before the notifications go out. If you were up to date, you were already covered.

#Linux #CyberSecurity #CVE #InfoSec #patchmanagement

There’s a fake CAPTCHA going around that tricks you into installing malware on your own computer. It works on Windows and Mac. And your antivirus won’t catch it, because you’re the one running it.

#hacking #cybersecurity #onlinesafety #captcha #techreels

Airbus just moved 900 critical apps off AWS and onto a French cloud provider. Big move. But the supply chain problem nobody’s talking about makes it way more complicated than the press release suggests.

via Rupert Goodwins / The Register

#digitalsovereignty #cybersecurity #cloud #aws #techreels

Two years ago today I was sitting in Heathrow watching the world stop. It wasn’t a cyberattack. It was a config file. And we still haven’t learned the right lesson. #cybersecurity #crowdstrike #techreels #securityawareness #infosec

Your password manager just taught your AI how to log in for you. Here’s why that’s more complicated than it sounds.

#cybersecurity #AI #1Password #Claude #techreels

Your robot vacuum has a camera, knows your floor plan, and stores your Wi-Fi password in plaintext. A security researcher found a flaw that lets someone use one Shark vacuum to spy on any other Shark vacuum in the same region. SharkNinja has known since March. Still unpatched. If yours is connected right now, the advice is simple: unplug it from Wi-Fi.

#cybersecurity #iotsecurity #privacy #sharkninja #techreels

A clock that thought it was 2006 took down Australia’s biggest mobile network. One unpatched server. One missing document. Millions of people offline. Here’s what actually happened.

#cybersecurity #telstra #infosec #techreels #networksecurity

A free blood pressure app wanted to share my data with 210 partners, including Meta, Google, and TikTok, before I’d logged a single reading. Free doesn’t mean nobody’s paying, it just means you’re not paying with money. #cybersecurity #dataprivacy #techtok #appsecurity #gdpr

A researcher promised Microsoft something “bone-shattering” back in June. Yesterday they delivered. A new Windows exploit dropped hours after the biggest Patch Tuesday in history, and none of those 622 patches cover it. #cybersecurity #windows #infosec #zeroday #techreels

Microsoft just blocked the biggest security update in history from reaching some Dell users. 622 vulnerabilities patched. Three zero-days. Two already being exploited. And a chunk of Dell machines that can’t get any of it yet because of a driver conflict nobody saw coming.

The AI arms race in vulnerability discovery is very real. And this month’s numbers prove it.

#cybersecurity #cyber #patchtuesday #microsoft #dell

There’s a UK app already live, paying subscribers to upload footage of arrests and emergencies, and it slipped straight past the new social media ban. Their own terms and conditions tell you everything. Credit to @dr_catherine_knibbs for first flagging this on TikTok. Full breakdown in the video.

#CyberNews #OnlineSafety #UKNews #digitalsafety #socialmediaban

Anthropic’s own AI agent can be hijacked to read your Gmail, and eight patches haven’t fixed it. Come on Anthropic, you were meant to be the good one!

#CyberSecurity #InfoSec #AI #DataPrivacy #Techreels

He scanned his entire company’s network for fun and blamed a virus when it broke. I’ve got a story that comes close. 

#CyberSecurity #TechNews #ITHumor #NetworkSecurity #techreels

DHS’s own information sharing network was breached and it took over a month to notice, right as the department runs security for the World Cup. Here’s what “unclassified” actually protects, and what it doesn’t.

#CyberSecurity #DataBreach #microsoft #DHS #techreels

Meta launched a tool to detect AI generated images. Reuters tested it and found a simple crop was enough to fool it over half the time. Here’s what that means for spotting fakes online.  #AI #Meta #Deepfakes #TechNews #techreels

We talk about how scammers quickly exploited the Venezuela earthquake by setting up fake donation websites, many asking for Bitcoin, and how this pattern repeats after disasters like Hurricane Harvey and COVID. We warn viewers to avoid crypto-only charity sites and suggest using legitimate charities, plus an idea for Google to add site reputation warnings. #earthquake #cybersecurity #scam #google #techreels

Dutch intelligence says Russian hackers hijacked civilian internet connected cameras, including doorbells, to spy on NATO weapons routes into Ukraine. No brand named, no sophisticated exploit needed, just default passwords and outdated firmware. If you’ve got cheap connected kit at home, this is your reminder to check it.

#CyberSecurity #Doorbell #ukraine #NATO #smarthome

A popular Chrome extension just got flagged as malware. 1.6 million installs, years of trust, one hidden module. Here’s what was actually inside it, and why nobody caught it sooner. Bye ModHeader!

#CyberSecurity #chrome #DataPrivacy #TechNews #webdev

AI scribes are saving doctors time. But is the consent real, or is it guilt dressed up as a yes? And why does your most private conversation of the year need to leave the room at all?

#NHS #AI #Consent #healthcare #Cyber

An AI is writing your doctor’s notes. In the US it’s already led to a lawsuit over fake consent. In the UK, it’s rolling out fast while the regulator meant to police it doesn’t currently have anyone in charge. Thanks to @thescouseoracle for asking the questions. 

#AI #NHS #DataPrivacy #healthcare #cyber
